title: Scheduled and background agents
trust_boundary: Before: a person starts each run, watches it and reads the result. After: runs start from a clock, an event or another system, with nobody watching, using credentials stored for the purpose.
Whatever fires the trigger (an incoming email, a webhook, a new issue, a dropped file) is input an outsider may be able to send.
Stored credentials outlive the session and sometimes the person who set the task up.
Results land somewhere and may be acted on later by people or automations that never saw the run.
context_questions: What starts a run: a schedule, an event, another agent? Who can cause that event?
Whose credentials does it run with, and when do they expire?
Who is told when a run fails or does something unusual, and who can stop it?

threats.title: A trigger an outsider can fire or shape
threats.description: An email, an issue, a webhook or a file starts a run and also supplies its instructions.
questions: Can someone outside the organisation cause the triggering event?
Is the triggering content treated as data, or as the task?
vendor_evidence: Controls on who or what may trigger.
no_standard_test: Event-triggered runs. The public injection benchmarks start from a user's request, not from an event.

threats.title: Standing credentials and permissions
threats.description: Long-lived tokens with broad scope sit in a task definition, and keep working after their owner has moved on.
questions: What can the stored credential do, and is that the least the task needs?
What happens to the task when its owner leaves or loses access?
vendor_evidence: How credentials for unattended runs are stored, scoped and rotated.

threats.title: Actions with nobody present to approve
threats.description: Approvals are granted in advance or skipped, so the agent's first mistake or manipulation takes effect.
questions: Which actions can an unattended run take, and which are held for a person?
How often does the agent do more than it was asked on ordinary tasks?
vendor_evidence: Rates of out-of-scope actions on benign tasks.
no_standard_test: Unattended operation of a given product. The one benchmark found covers coding agents on benign tasks.

threats.title: A changed task or a delayed instruction keeps running
threats.description: A schedule, a task definition or the agent's configuration is altered once and the change executes every time after.
questions: Who can edit a task or the agent's configuration, and is every change logged and reviewed?
Can a run modify its own schedule, prompt or configuration?
vendor_evidence: Change control and audit for task definitions.

threats.title: Runaway runs
threats.description: Loops, retries and fan-out consume budget or repeat an action many times.
questions: What caps run time, frequency, retries and spend?
Does an alert reach a person?

threats.title: Nobody notices
threats.description: Failures, drift after a model update and misbehaviour go unseen because no one reads the output of a job that usually works.
questions: Who reviews run results, and how often?
Is the model version pinned, and who is told when it changes?

threats.title: Stopping it
threats.description: No clear way, or no clear owner, to pause or remove a task quickly.
questions: Who can pause, edit and delete a task? Is there one place that lists them all?
How fast does a stop take effect on a run in progress?
no_standard_test: No standard test. Record what is in place.
